name: search-hub.research
purpose: One federated project-research call at a named effort level (fast, standard, deep), returning bounded ranked rows plus routing meta and a verdict the skill branches on.

effort.description: fast: classifier, limit 5; standard: classifier, limit 10; deep: every active provider, limit 20. Rows returned are capped at 6; ranked_count carries the total.

types.description: Explicit leaf-type tokens; the vocabulary of record is `search-hub providers list --json` `.providers[].type` (the program library is `library`). Overrides the classifier and the deep fan-out.

group.description: Scope the fan-out to one scenario's leaves.

scope.description: Optional corpus facet passed to scoped providers.

include_skill.description: Search only the skill corpus and return the selected skill's content through Prompt Manager.

include_discover.description: Run Prompt Manager discover on the same query; may be used without reading a skill body.

capture_note.description: Explicitly append one query-record containing only the verdict and counts; requires include_discover=true and an authorized memory write.

repeat_after_status.description: Run the same query, read Search Hub lifecycle status once, then repeat once if it is running.

assumptions: search-hub is running and search-hub/query/query is reachable from the kernel
the kernel passes `type` as a list of strings; a comma-joined string is refused by the proto encoder
the caller treats status unavailable as unknown and zero_result as a verdict, never as failure
when the router's reranker leg is absent the response has no fused `ranked` rows and every hit is in meta `groups[].hits`; the program reads them from the same call
invariants: exactly one Search Hub query by default; repeat_after_status makes exactly two identical queries with one lifecycle status read between them
Memory is written only when capture_note=true; the single appended query-record is generated from verdict/count metadata and never stores query text, result snippets or skill content
the groups field is read from the final Search Hub query's meta()
skill lookup searches only the skill type, calls only the declared Prompt Manager discovery/read bindings and returns one skill body capped at 8500 UTF-8 bytes
ranked rows are at most 6 with snippets cut to 60 characters; nothing else is materialized; the envelope stays under the 4 KB stdout bound
a reranker outage with usable hits is verdict answered_degraded with class reranker_absent; it is never zero_result and never sets escalate_to_web
zero hits with a degraded or partial provider leg are unavailable, preserve the provider degradation reason, and never claim a clean zero or escalate as one
the envelope is printed exactly once, on every path

bindings.note: Used only when repeat_after_status=true; the route exposes lifecycle status only.
Used only when capture_note=true after successful discovery; requires explicit write authority.

signals.verdict: one of answered, answered_degraded, zero_result, no_provider_selected, unavailable
signals.ranked: at most 6 hits (5 for fast) as {id,title,provider_id,type,path,score,rerank_score,snippet}; snippets cut to 60 characters so the envelope fits the 4 KB stdout bound
signals.ranked_count: count of hits: the fused ranked rows, or every groups[].hits entry when ranked is empty
signals.ranked_source: ranked when the rows are the router's fused list; groups when they were read from groups[].hits (reranker absent) and are ordered by provider score
signals.corpora_searched: first 6 provider ids the router searched
signals.corpora_count: count of provider ids the router searched
signals.providers_hit: provider id to count among the returned rows
signals.routing_degrade_reason: router's degrade reason, or a bounded degraded provider note when the router omits one
signals.partial: some provider legs had not answered within the timeout
signals.pending_providers: count of legs still pending when partial
signals.latency_ms: federated latency of this query as an integer (cast from the protojson int64 string)
signals.reranker_leg: which reranker ordered the rows; none when the leg is absent
signals.escalate_to_web: true only when the verdict is zero_result or no_provider_selected and web was not among the types; unavailable is not a completed negative
signals.skill_lookup: null unless include_skill=true; then {status,source,id,content,truncated} for one read skill, with content capped at 8500 UTF-8 bytes and partial status when capped
signals.skill_discovery: null unless include_discover=true; then status and matched_count only
signals.memory_capture: null unless capture_note=true; then status and optional opaque entry_ref only, never the note body
signals.status_check: null unless repeat_after_status=true; then one lifecycle status value from before the repeated query
signals.first_query: null unless repeat_after_status=true and the status was running; then ranked_count and corpora_count from the first query

inputs.query: how does search hub route queries
how to discover a task skill

fixtures.note: Skill lookup fails before any binding call when the explicit type excludes skills.
Rejects the memory write option unless Prompt Manager discovery is explicitly selected.
With the reranker leg absent this returns partial, verdict answered_degraded, ranked_source groups; it must not return zero_result.
